engagement_name: Customer Churn Reduction Platform — NorthStar Telecom
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0301

Client: NorthStar Telecom BV
Contoso Consulting Practice: Insights & Data
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 18 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will design, build and operationalise a machine-learning-powered Customer Churn Prediction and Intervention Platform for NorthStar Telecom's residential broadband division. The platform will ingest real-time usage telemetry, CRM event data and customer service interaction logs to produce daily propensity-to-churn scores at the individual customer level. A next-best-action recommendation engine will surface targeted retention offers to the contact centre and digital self-service channels within 24 hours of a risk threshold being breached.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
The engagement is structured around three primary outcome KPIs, each with a confirmed baseline measured over the 12-month period ending 31 December 2025:
  (a) Voluntary churn rate: reduce from 2.8% per month to ≤2.0% per month across the residential broadband base, measured on a rolling 90-day average by the end of Month 12 post-go-live.
  (b) Retention offer acceptance rate: achieve ≥34% acceptance on AI-surfaced retention interventions, versus the current 19% on manually selected offers.
  (c) Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) uplift: deliver a ≥€4.2M incremental CLV improvement across the intervention cohort within 18 months, verified by an independent measurement partner using a randomised holdout group.
Baseline data has been independently verified by NorthStar's analytics team and agreed in writing. A measurement methodology document, including holdout group design and attribution rules, will be co-signed at contract execution.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Contoso Consulting's fees are structured as follows: a fixed build fee of €1.85M covering Months 1–6 (platform design, model development, integration, UAT), and a performance fee of up to €1.2M payable in two tranches at Month 12 and Month 18, contingent on achievement of outcome KPIs (a) and (c) above. The performance fee is calculated pro-rata against target achievement; partial payment applies if KPIs are met at 80–99% of target. If churn reduction exceeds the target by ≥15%, a shared gain clause applies and NorthStar will pay an additional success bonus of €300K. Both parties have reviewed and accepted this structure; legal sign-off is pending commercial close.

4. GOVERNANCE AND MEASUREMENT
A joint Outcome Review Board will convene monthly, co-chaired by Contoso Consulting's Engagement Director and NorthStar's Chief Customer Officer. Outcome measurement will use NorthStar's existing Salesforce and Snowflake infrastructure; Contoso Consulting will not have write access to production systems. An escrow account holding 20% of the performance fee will be released upon third-party audit confirmation.

engagement_name: Finance Shared Services Transformation — Meridian Pharma Group
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0302

Client: Meridian Pharma Group plc
Contoso Consulting Practice: Business Services
Contract Type: Time & Materials
Engagement Duration: 24 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will provide a team of finance transformation consultants and technology specialists to support Meridian Pharma Group's global Finance Shared Services Centre (FSSC) migration programme. The engagement covers process redesign for Order-to-Cash, Purchase-to-Pay and Record-to-Report towers across seven European entities. Contoso Consulting resources will be embedded within the client programme management office on a day-rate basis. The scope explicitly excludes any post-go-live operational responsibility.

2. DELIVERABLES
Deliverables are defined as process maps (current and future state), system configuration documents, data migration scripts, test scripts, and training materials. Acceptance criteria are technical: client sign-off on each deliverable within 10 business days of submission. There are no post-implementation performance targets defined in the SoW, and no KPIs linked to business outcomes such as days sales outstanding (DSO), cost per transaction or error rates. Meridian's Group CFO has explicitly stated that no outcome-linked payment terms will be accepted, citing the company's procurement policy which prohibits contingent fee arrangements with third-party technology vendors pending an ongoing internal audit review.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
All Contoso Consulting resources will be billed at agreed day rates per grade (Partner: €2,800/day; Principal Consultant: €2,200/day; Senior Consultant: €1,650/day; Analyst: €950/day). Travel and expenses are reimbursed at cost with a 10% administrative uplift. The contract includes a 3-month rolling termination clause on either side. Total contract value is estimated at €6.4M over 24 months, subject to actual days consumed.

4. CONSTRAINTS
The client's Group Internal Audit function is conducting a review of all third-party vendor arrangements exceeding €1M. Until this review concludes (estimated Q3 2026), no contract amendments that introduce risk-sharing, performance-linked pricing or gain-share mechanisms will be considered by Meridian's legal team. Contoso Consulting's commercial team has noted this constraint and confirmed it renders outcome-based pricing structurally infeasible for this engagement at this time.

STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0303

Client: Vanguard Insurance NV
Contoso Consulting Practice: Financial Services
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 12 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will redesign and automate Vanguard Insurance's end-to-end motor claims intake and triage process. The solution will combine intelligent document processing (IDP) to extract structured data from FNOL submissions, a rules-based triage engine to route low-complexity claims to straight-through processing (STP), and an AI-assisted damage assessment module integrated with Vanguard's existing Guidewire ClaimCenter platform. Human-in-the-loop review will be retained for all claims above €15,000 in estimated settlement value.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
Outcome KPIs with confirmed baselines (average over 2024 fiscal year):
  (a) Straight-through processing rate: increase from 31% to ≥55% of eligible motor claims by end of Month 10.
  (b) Average claims cycle time: reduce from 11.4 days to ≤6 days for STP-eligible claims, measured as FNOL receipt to settlement authorisation.
  (c) Customer satisfaction (CSAT) on claims journey: achieve ≥4.1/5.0 on the post-settlement survey (current baseline: 3.6/5.0), measured over a rolling 60-day window from Month 8 onwards.
Baseline data sourced from Vanguard's BI platform; methodology agreed. Independent measurement via Vanguard's existing Medallia survey infrastructure.
Note: KPI (c) measurement tooling is in place, however the survey question weighting for the digital channel has not yet been finalised. This represents a minor gap that Contoso Consulting proposes to resolve during the Discovery phase.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Fixed fee of €980K for platform build (Months 1–7). A performance uplift of €240K is payable at Month 12 contingent on achieving KPIs (a) and (b) simultaneously. KPI (c) is a satisfaction threshold; failure to meet it triggers a €60K service credit against the Month 12 invoice. The client's Chief Claims Officer and CFO have approved the commercial structure in principle; final sign-off is at board level in May 2026.

4. GOVERNANCE
Monthly outcome review calls between Contoso Consulting Delivery Lead and Vanguard's Head of Claims Operations. Quarterly steering committee with CFO attendance. All outcome measurements will be conducted by Vanguard's independent analytics team with Contoso Consulting observer rights.

engagement_name: Digital Twin Factory Operations — Heidel Manufacturing
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0304

Client: Heidel Manufacturing GmbH
Contoso Consulting Practice: Digital Manufacturing
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 24 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will develop and deploy a Digital Twin solution for Heidel Manufacturing's flagship production facility in Stuttgart, covering 8 CNC machining lines and 3 assembly cells. The Digital Twin will integrate real-time sensor data from 1,400+ IoT endpoints via an Azure IoT Hub ingestion pipeline into a PTC ThingWorx model layer, with a live visualisation and anomaly detection dashboard accessible to shift supervisors and central engineering. A predictive maintenance module will generate work orders in SAP PM automatically when degradation thresholds are breached.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
  (a) Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE): improve from confirmed baseline of 71.4% to ≥82% across the 8 CNC lines within 18 months of go-live. OEE is measured weekly using Heidel's existing MES data.
  (b) Unplanned downtime incidents: reduce from an average of 23 incidents/month to ≤12 incidents/month by Month 18, measured from SAP PM work order data.
  (c) Scrap and rework cost: achieve ≥18% reduction in monthly scrap cost (current baseline: €187K/month) by Month 18, verified by Heidel's finance controller.
  (d) Maintenance cost per machine per year: reduce from €41K to ≤€33K by the end of the 24-month contract period.
All baselines have been independently validated. A measurement protocol document has been agreed and co-signed. Heidel's engineering team has committed a dedicated data integration resource for the first 6 months.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Phase 1 (Months 1–9): Fixed build and integration fee of €2.1M. Phase 2 (Months 10–24): Annual performance fee of up to €850K, structured as quarterly payments calculated against OEE and downtime KPI achievement (KPIs a and b carry 40% weight each; KPI c carries 20%). If OEE exceeds 85%, a stretch bonus of €150K applies. The commercial model has been reviewed and approved by Heidel's Board of Directors.

4. DATA AND INTEGRATION
Heide will provide API access to MES and SAP PM systems. Contoso Consulting will deploy edge compute nodes on-premises; all data remains within Heidel's sovereign cloud boundary. A data processing agreement (DPA) has been executed.

engagement_name: Workforce Analytics Platform — Albrecht Retail Group
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0305

Client: Albrecht Retail Group SE
Contoso Consulting Practice: People & Organisation
Contract Type: Time & Materials
Engagement Duration: 12 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will deliver a Workforce Analytics platform for Albrecht Retail Group's HR function, covering 28,000 employees across 6 European markets. The platform will integrate data from Workday HCM, the client's payroll system and 14 regional time-tracking tools to produce dashboards on headcount, attrition, absenteeism and workforce cost. The engagement also includes a capability-building programme for 15 HR business partners.

2. OUTCOMES AND MEASUREMENT
The SoW references the following desired outcomes: 'improve workforce visibility', 'reduce time to insight for HR decisions' and 'support strategic workforce planning'. No baseline measurements have been provided for any of these goals. The client's CHRO has indicated that baseline data collection is planned but will not be available until Q3 2026, after the platform is expected to be live. Specific KPI targets (e.g. reduction in time-to-fill, attrition rate improvement, HR cost ratio) were discussed in the discovery phase but were not included in the final SoW at the client's request because 'the business is not yet ready to commit to specific numbers'. No measurement methodology or holdout design has been agreed.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Contoso Consulting will be remunerated on a T&M basis at standard day rates. Total estimated contract value is €1.9M. There are no performance-linked fees, milestone bonuses or outcome clauses in the current commercial structure. The client explicitly declined Contoso Consulting's proposal to include an outcome-linked element, citing organisational change fatigue following a recent ERP programme.

4. NOTE FROM COMMERCIAL TEAM
Contoso Consulting's commercial director flagged this engagement as a candidate for outcome-based repricing in the next contract renewal cycle (Month 12+), contingent on the client agreeing to baseline measurement during the initial platform deployment phase. This is not reflected in the current SoW.

engagement_name: Supply Chain Control Tower — Fortuna Consumer Goods
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0306

Client: Fortuna Consumer Goods NV
Contoso Consulting Practice: Supply Chain & Operations
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 15 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will implement an end-to-end Supply Chain Control Tower for Fortuna Consumer Goods across its Western European distribution network (12 distribution centres, 4 manufacturing plants, 340 Tier-1 suppliers). The Control Tower will integrate demand sensing signals, supplier lead-time feeds, logistics track-and-trace data and inventory positions into a unified operational view. AI-driven exception management will surface supply risk events 5–10 days earlier than Fortuna's current process, enabling proactive intervention.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
  (a) Perfect Order Rate: improve from baseline 87.3% to ≥93% within 12 months of go-live, measured monthly across all European orders.
  (b) Inventory holding cost reduction: achieve ≥12% reduction in average inventory days-on-hand (current: 38 days) across all 12 DCs by Month 12.
  (c) Supply disruption response time: reduce mean time from disruption detection to corrective action from 4.2 days to ≤1.5 days, measured from event log data in SAP TM.
  (d) Logistics cost per case: reduce from €0.83 to ≤€0.74 by Month 15, verified by Fortuna's finance team.
All baselines confirmed from Fortuna's SAP S/4HANA and TM systems. Independent measurement by Fortuna's Group Supply Chain Analytics team.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Fixed platform build fee: €1.65M (Months 1–6). Performance fee: up to €750K payable at Month 12 and Month 15 based on achievement of KPIs (a), (b) and (d), weighted 40%/30%/30% respectively. KPI (c) is a service level threshold — missing it for two consecutive months triggers a €45K service credit. Gain-share: if Perfect Order Rate exceeds 95%, an additional bonus of €100K applies. Board-level approval received from Fortuna's Group Executive Committee.

4. DEPENDENCIES
Fortuna will provide a dedicated integration team for SAP connectivity. A data governance framework for supplier data sharing is being finalised; Contoso Consulting has reviewed the draft and confirms it is fit for purpose. Three Tier-1 suppliers have already signed data-sharing consent forms.

engagement_name: Cloud Infrastructure Managed Services — Berova Financial Services
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0307

Client: Berova Financial Services Ltd
Contoso Consulting Practice: Cloud Infrastructure & Security
Contract Type: Fixed Retainer (Managed Services)
Engagement Duration: 36 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will provide Level 1–3 managed services for Berova Financial Services' Azure cloud estate, covering approximately 340 virtual machines, 8 AKS clusters, a Cosmos DB tier and associated networking components. Services include 24/7 monitoring, incident management, patching, capacity management and monthly architecture review. The engagement is governed by a Service Management framework aligned to ITIL v4.

2. SERVICE LEVELS AND MEASUREMENT
SLAs are defined for platform availability (99.7% monthly uptime for production workloads), incident response times (P1: 15 minutes; P2: 1 hour; P3: 4 hours) and change success rate (≥97%). Penalty credits apply at the rate of 5% of monthly fees per 0.1% availability shortfall below SLA. No business outcome KPIs are included in the contract. Berova's CTO confirmed in the commercial negotiation that the bank's risk and procurement policies prohibit outcome-based pricing for infrastructure managed services, as the bank does not consider infrastructure uptime to be a direct driver of revenue or customer outcomes that can be independently attributed to a single vendor.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Monthly fixed retainer of €185,000 covering all in-scope services up to 8,000 managed service units (MSUs) per month. Consumption above 8,000 MSUs is billed at €18/MSU. Annual price indexation at CPI. The retainer model was specifically requested by Berova's procurement team; Contoso Consulting's proposal to include an outcome-linked component (e.g., cloud cost optimisation savings share) was declined.

4. REGULATORY CONTEXT
Berova is regulated by the Dutch Central Bank (DNB) and the UK PRA. All outsourcing arrangements must comply with EBA outsourcing guidelines and PRA SS2/21. These regulations require that service levels be defined in absolute, measurable terms — which the current SLA framework satisfies. Outcome-based pricing was assessed by Berova's legal team as creating regulatory ambiguity and was excluded on that basis.

STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0308

Client: Castellan Energy plc
Contoso Consulting Practice: Procurement & Supply Chain
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 18 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will deliver an AI-Powered Procurement Optimisation programme for Castellan Energy covering the company's indirect spend categories (IT, facilities, professional services, logistics) totalling approximately £380M per annum. The programme includes spend analytics, supplier rationalisation, AI-assisted sourcing event management, contract compliance monitoring and a supplier performance management framework. Contoso Consulting will work alongside Castellan's 45-person procurement team, not replace it.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
All targets agreed with Castellan's Group CPO and CFO, with baselines drawn from the 2024/25 fiscal year:
  (a) Addressable spend savings: deliver ≥£18M in verified, recurring annual savings across in-scope categories by Month 15. Savings will be validated by Castellan's finance team using a standard savings methodology document agreed at contract execution.
  (b) Supplier base rationalisation: reduce active suppliers in scope from 2,847 to ≤1,600 by Month 12, with ≥90% spend consolidation to preferred suppliers.
  (c) Contract compliance rate: improve purchase-order-backed spend from 61% to ≥82% by Month 15, measured from SAP Ariba data.
  (d) Sourcing cycle time: reduce average competitive tender cycle from 74 days to ≤40 days by Month 12.
Savings validation methodology is co-signed. Baselines are confirmed from SAP Ariba and Castellan finance systems.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Contoso Consulting's fee is structured as a retained advisory fee of £420K for Months 1–6 (diagnostic and strategy phase), followed by a success-based fee of 8% of verified Year 1 savings delivered above a £6M floor, payable quarterly from Month 9 onwards. The success fee is capped at £3.2M over the engagement term. This structure directly aligns Contoso Consulting's economic incentive with Castellan's procurement value realisation. Approved by Castellan's Executive Committee.

4. GOVERNANCE
A Savings Governance Board (SGB) co-chaired by Contoso Consulting's Programme Director and Castellan's CPO will meet monthly to review savings pipeline, validation status and contract compliance. All savings claims require dual sign-off from Castellan Finance and a named category manager before being counted against the success fee threshold.

engagement_name: SAP S/4HANA Greenfield Rollout — Delvaux Industrial Group
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0309

Client: Delvaux Industrial Group SA
Contoso Consulting Practice: Enterprise Applications
Contract Type: Fixed Price
Engagement Duration: 30 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will lead the full lifecycle delivery of a SAP S/4HANA 2023 greenfield implementation for Delvaux Industrial Group, replacing legacy ERP systems across 9 legal entities in Belgium, France, Germany and Poland. The programme covers Finance (FI/CO), Procurement (MM/SRM), Manufacturing (PP/QM/PM), Sales (SD), and Group Reporting. The engagement is structured as a fixed-price programme with a defined scope baseline and change control process.

2. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AND DELIVERABLES
The contract defines acceptance criteria that are entirely technical and functional in nature: system performance benchmarks (peak load processing ≤3 seconds for standard transactions), data migration accuracy (≥99.5% record-level match on validated data set), functional test pass rate (≥95% of agreed test scripts), and user training completion rate (≥90% of named users). No business outcome KPIs are included in the SoW. Measurable post-go-live business outcomes (e.g., reduction in period-end close cycle, improvement in inventory accuracy, reduction in purchase price variance) were proposed by Contoso Consulting during the sales cycle but were rejected by Delvaux's procurement team on the grounds that the SAP programme is primarily a compliance and infrastructure upgrade, and business outcomes are dependent on post-programme change management activities outside of Contoso Consulting's scope.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Fixed-price contract of €14.7M, payable against 8 defined project milestones. A 10% retention is held until 90 days post go-live acceptance. Contoso Consulting carries delivery risk under the fixed-price model; any overrun is absorbed by Contoso Consulting. There is a contractual provision for scope change, but the change control process requires approval from Delvaux's Programme Board. No outcome-linked fees, gain-share or performance bonuses are included or permitted under the current commercial terms.

4. REGULATORY AND ORGANISATIONAL CONSTRAINTS
Delvaux's Belgian operations are subject to GDPR and NIS2 requirements that constrain data access arrangements. The programme's steering committee includes a member of the works council (Belgian co-determination requirement), which adds change management complexity. Contoso Consulting's legal review confirms that introducing outcome-based pricing into this contract would require a full renegotiation of the fixed-price terms and approval from Delvaux's supervisory board — a process estimated to take 6–9 months.

STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0310

Client: Solaris Bank AG
Contoso Consulting Practice: Customer Experience & Digital
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 12 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will redesign and digitise the end-to-end onboarding journey for Solaris Bank's SME banking product, covering business current account opening, KYC/AML document collection and initial credit assessment. The redesigned journey will replace a 14-step paper-assisted process with a fully digital self-service flow, supported by automated document verification (eIDAS-compliant), open banking data ingestion for financial health assessment, and an AI-assisted credit decisioning model. The solution will be deployed on Solaris's existing AWS infrastructure.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
Baselines confirmed from Solaris Bank's 2025 operational data:
  (a) Time-to-account-open: reduce from 8.3 business days to ≤2 business days for ≥70% of SME applications by Month 9.
  (b) Onboarding abandonment rate: reduce from 44% to ≤22% of initiated applications by Month 9.
  (c) KYC straight-through rate: increase from 28% to ≥55% of submitted KYC packs requiring no manual intervention, measured over a rolling 30-day period.
  (d) Net Promoter Score (NPS) for onboarding journey: improve from +12 to ≥+38, measured via in-app survey (current sample: 320 responses/month; target: ≥500 responses/month with statistical significance confirmed).
Note: KPI (d) has a sample size dependency — achieving statistical significance at ≥+38 requires volume growth in the SME book. Contoso Consulting has flagged this as a measurement risk and proposed a fallback metric (CSAT ≥4.3/5) if NPS sample remains below threshold.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Discovery and design phase (Months 1–3): fixed fee €380K. Build and test phase (Months 4–8): fixed fee €720K. Performance period (Months 9–12): outcome-based fee of up to €340K tied to KPIs (a), (b) and (c) at 40%/30%/30% weighting. KPI (d) acts as a satisfaction guardrail; failure triggers a €50K service credit. Total contract value up to €1.44M. Approved by Solaris Bank's COO and CFO.

4. REGULATORY AND COMPLIANCE
All AI models used in credit decisioning will comply with EU AI Act requirements (high-risk AI system classification). An AI model card and explainability report will be produced for regulatory submission. Contoso Consulting's AI Ethics team will conduct a bias assessment prior to go-live.

Contoso Consulting will build a customer lifetime value (CLV) prediction platform for a major telecom operator. Success is defined by a 12% reduction in voluntary churn within 18 months of go-live, measured against a control cohort. The platform must achieve ≥80% model accuracy on a held-out test set. Revenue-at-risk KPIs are included. Payments are milestone-based with a final outcome payment tied to the churn reduction target.

engagement_name: Legacy Mainframe Migration — Public Sector Bank
sow_text: Contoso Consulting will migrate 14 COBOL-based mainframe applications to a cloud-native microservices architecture for a government-owned bank. The engagement is billed T&M at agreed senior rates. There are no outcome KPIs defined; deliverables are completed migration sprints and test sign-off documents. No SLA-linked performance targets exist post-migration. Regulatory constraints prevent any revenue-sharing or outcome-based payment clauses.

Contoso Consulting will deliver a predictive maintenance solution for wind turbine assets. Target: reduce unplanned downtime by 25% and cut maintenance cost per turbine by €8,000/year within 12 months. KPIs are well-defined and baseline data is available. Payments are split: 60% fixed milestone, 40% outcome-linked. The client has committed a dedicated data team and historical sensor data for three years.

Contoso Consulting will automate HR shared services processes (onboarding, payroll queries, leave management) for a global pharmaceutical company. Target outcomes are defined but vague: 'reduce HR transaction time' and 'improve employee satisfaction'. No baseline metrics are provided, no agreed measurement methodology, and the client has not confirmed data access. The commercial model is time-and-materials.

Contoso Consulting will lead a 12-month omnichannel transformation for a premium fashion retailer, integrating in-store, e-commerce, and mobile channels. Success KPIs: increase online revenue contribution from 28% to 40%, reduce cart abandonment by 15%, achieve NPS ≥55 on digital journeys. All KPIs have baselines confirmed and measurement tooling is in place. Contract includes a shared-gain clause if revenue targets are exceeded.

engagement_name: Cybersecurity Managed Detection & Response — Financial Services
sow_text: Contoso Consulting will provide a 24/7 Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service for a regional bank. The engagement is priced on a fixed monthly retainer. SLA KPIs cover mean time to detect (MTTD ≤15 min) and mean time to respond (MTTR ≤60 min) for critical incidents. Business outcome targets (fraud loss reduction, regulatory fine avoidance) are not included in the commercial model. The client declined outcome-linked pricing citing insurance policy constraints.

Contoso Consulting will design and implement a data mesh architecture for a consumer packaged goods company operating in 22 markets. Outcomes defined: reduce time-to-insight for marketing analytics from 5 days to 4 hours, enable self-serve data access for 200+ business users. Baseline measurements exist. However, the SoW does not specify how outcome achievement will be independently verified, and there is no escrow or holdback mechanism for the outcome payment.

Contoso Consulting will implement an AI-powered contact centre platform for a water utility. KPIs: deflect 35% of inbound calls to self-service channels, reduce average handling time by 20%, achieve CSAT ≥4.0/5. Baseline confirmed. A pilot phase will validate deflection rates before full rollout. Contract is structured with an initial fixed fee for build and a 24-month outcome-linked maintenance fee tied to CSAT and deflection targets.

Contoso Consulting will upgrade an aerospace manufacturer's Oracle ERP from R12 to Oracle Cloud. Scope includes chart-of-accounts redesign, intercompany reconciliation automation, and consolidation reporting. The engagement is fixed-price. No post-go-live business outcome KPIs are included; acceptance criteria are technical (system performance, data migration accuracy). Outcome-based pricing was proposed by Contoso Consulting but rejected by the client procurement team.

Contoso Consulting will build a supplier risk intelligence platform ingesting ESG, financial health, and geopolitical signals for a tier-1 automotive OEM. Target: reduce supplier-related supply chain disruptions by 30% within 18 months and achieve a supplier risk score coverage of 95% of Tier-1 suppliers. KPIs are clear and measurable with agreed baselines. The client is open to a gain-sharing model if the disruption reduction target is met.

Contoso Consulting will develop a digital twin for a smart factory floor covering 6 production lines. Outcomes: increase overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 72% to 82%, reduce scrap rate by 18%. Baselines are confirmed. The SoW includes quarterly outcome reviews and a bonus payment structure. The client has existing IoT infrastructure and has allocated a cross-functional team. The commercial model is partially outcome-based with a fixed build fee and a 3-year performance fee.

engagement_name: Tax Compliance Automation — Professional Services Firm
sow_text: Contoso Consulting will automate corporate tax compliance workflows for a Big Four professional services firm. Deliverables are process maps, RPA bots, and a compliance dashboard. The engagement is T&M. No outcome targets are defined beyond 'improved efficiency'. The client explicitly stated they do not want outcome-linked commercial terms because internal audit rules prohibit contingent fee arrangements with technology vendors.

Contoso Consulting will deliver a 6-month supply chain optimisation programme for a tier-1 retailer. The scope includes demand forecasting model development, inventory reorder logic redesign, and integration with the client's ERP system. Success is measured by a 15% reduction in out-of-stock events and a 10% reduction in holding costs by end of programme. Monthly KPI review sessions are included. The contract is priced on a fixed-fee basis.

Contoso Consulting will provide ongoing managed services for a mid-size insurance company covering network operations, server monitoring, and level-2 helpdesk. The engagement is billed on a time-and-materials basis at agreed day rates. There are no defined business outcome targets or SLA-linked KPIs beyond standard uptime (99.5%). Contract duration is 24 months with a 3-month notice period.

Contoso Consulting will redesign and automate the end-to-end claims intake and triage process for a global insurer. Target outcomes: reduce average claims processing time from 14 days to 5 days, reduce manual touchpoints by 60%, and achieve a customer satisfaction score of ≥4.2/5 on claims interactions. The project will run for 9 months. Acceptance criteria and milestone payments are partially defined but KPIs for the satisfaction score are missing.

Contoso Consulting will lead an SAP S/4HANA rollout for a European manufacturing group across 4 plants. The engagement is scoped as a fixed-price project. Business outcomes are not explicitly defined; deliverables are system go-live, data migration, and user training completion. No measurable post-go-live KPIs are included in the SoW. The contract has a regulatory compliance requirement preventing outcome-linked payment structures.
